findings.issue_text: [BUG] The migration calls execute(...)[0]['id'] on a query whose result set is empty on any install where the embed_category site setting has never been set (all fresh installs), crashing the migration with NoMethodError on nil. db:migrate fails for every new install (no 'embed_category' row exists, so the INNER JOIN returns zero rows and [0] is nil), blocking deployment entirely; the `if category_id == 0` fallback is unreachable because the code crashes before reaching it.

[BUG] update and destroy call save_host(host)/host.destroy on a record fetched with where(id: params[:id]).first without a nil check, so a missing or already-deleted id raises NoMethodError on nil. PUT/DELETE /admin/embeddable_hosts/:nonexistent_id returns a 500 instead of a 404; a double-delete from the UI (e.g. stale row after another admin removed it) hits this.

[BUG] Admin::EmbeddingController#update never reads params or mutates @embedding; it re-renders the fetch_embedding snapshot unchanged, so the PUT /admin/customize/embedding endpoint the frontend's saveChanges action calls is a silent no-op. An admin who changes embedding-level settings and clicks save gets a success response while nothing is persisted; combined with the client controller sending update({}), the update route exists purely to satisfy the adapter and stores no data.

[BUG] The INSERT interpolates the raw site-setting value h into SQL via string interpolation ("VALUES ('#{h}', ..."), so a host entry containing a single quote aborts the migration with a PG syntax error. Any site whose old embeddable_hosts setting contains a malformed/quoted entry fails db:migrate mid-migration, leaving the table half-populated and the transaction-dependent DELETE of the old settings never executed.

[ADVISORY] In the plural branch of _hydrateEmbedded, obj[k].map is called with no null guard and the trailing `|| []` is dead code (map never returns a falsy value), so a *_ids key serialized as null by the REST serializer raises TypeError on null.map. Any model whose embedded has-many is serialized with a null ids array (rather than []) crashes the store hydration path for the whole payload, breaking the admin page that loads it; the `hydrated || []` fallback gives false confidence that the empty case is handled.

[ADVISORY] saveChanges calls this.get('embedding').update({}) with an empty payload, so the save button wired into the update endpoint persists nothing and depends entirely on the no-op server handler to appear to succeed. Admins clicking any embedding-level save in the UI silently lose their action; the next change to this controller that assumes update persists state will be built on a path that provably writes nothing.

[ADVISORY] TopicEmbed.import now derives the category from EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(url), but when the record is absent (returns false) eh.try(:category_id) yields nil and the topic lands in uncategorized with no logging, unlike the old embed_category default which was an explicit operator setting. Sites that relied on embed_category for feed-embedded topics get all new embeds dumped into uncategorized once a feed URL's host has no EmbeddableHost row, silently changing post placement for every retrieved feed item.

[BUG] The migration crashes with NoMethodError on any site that never set the embed_category site setting, because `execute(...)[0]['id'].to_i` indexes into an empty result array. On every existing install without an embed_category row (the vast majority), the `[0]` returns nil and `nil['id']` raises, failing the migration and blocking deploy; the fallback `if category_id == 0` branch is dead code because the crash happens before it.

[BUG] The host values migrated from the old embeddable_hosts setting are interpolated directly into a SQL string (`VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`), so any stored host containing a single quote breaks the INSERT and the migration also becomes an injection vector. A user-saved host like `o'brien.example.com` (the old setting was freeform text) makes the migration fail mid-run after the table is created but before the site settings are deleted, leaving a half-migrated state.

[ADVISORY] The `update` action accepts a PUT and returns the serialized embedding but never persists any request parameters, making it a silent no-op endpoint, and the admin-embedding controller's saveChanges action still calls it. Any admin who wires a future editable field into the Embedding UI (the saveChanges action already exists in admin-embedding.js.es6 line 7) gets a success response while their changes are silently discarded.

[BUG] The validation regex explicitly permits a port suffix (`(:[0-9]{1,5})?`) but `record_for_host` matches on `uri.host`, which excludes the port, so a host saved with a port can never be matched. An admin who enters `eviltrout.com:3000` passes validation and appears saved, but embed requests from that origin (referer `http://eviltrout.com:3000/...`, uri.host `eviltrout.com`) are rejected with invalid referer host — the exact scenario the 'multiple hosts' spec in embed_controller_spec claims to cover but doesn't, since no spec creates a host with a port.

[ADVISORY] In the new `_ids` hydration branch, `hydrated || []` is dead code (a .map result is never nil) and individual `_lookupSubType` misses are still pushed into the array, so a payload whose root omits one referenced id yields an array containing an undefined element instead of an empty/skipped value. The next developer consuming a *_ids hydration where the side-loaded root is incomplete (e.g. a serializer that forgets to include one record) gets `undefined` array elements that crash on `.get('id')` at render time instead of a detectable empty result.

[ADVISORY] TopicEmbed.import now takes the category from the matched EmbeddableHost record, so when `record_for_host(url)` misses (eh is nil) the topic silently falls to the default category, replacing the old explicit embed_category behavior with no error or test covering the unmatched-host case. An operator polling a feed whose URL host is not in the embeddable_hosts table gets topics created in Uncategorized instead of any intended category, with no log line indicating the mismatch.

[ADVISORY] `create_table :embeddable_hosts, force: true` silently drops any pre-existing embeddable_hosts table during migration instead of failing loudly. If a prior partial run of this same migration already created and populated the table (plausible given the migration crashes on the nil embed_category row above before cleanup), the retry destroys the already-migrated host rows and re-runs with site settings already deleted, losing all configured hosts permanently.

[BUG] The `update` action performs no update — it re-fetches and re-serializes the embedding without reading any params, so `saveChanges` in the client (admin-embedding.js.es6 `this.get('embedding').update({})`) is a silent no-op write path. Any admin who clicks a save control wired to this endpoint gets a success response while nothing is persisted; the PUT /admin/customize/embedding route exists in config/routes.rb but no setting can ever be changed through it, an undocumented ships-inert endpoint.

[BUG] The `update` and `destroy` actions call `save_host(host)` / `host.destroy` on a record fetched with `where(id: params[:id]).first` without a nil guard, so a nonexistent or already-deleted id raises NoMethodError on nil. A PUT or DELETE to /admin/embeddable_hosts/:id with a stale id (double-click delete after the first request succeeded) returns a 500 instead of the 404 the REST contract implies; staff hit an error page instead of a graceful response.

[BUG] The migration inserts raw values from the old `embeddable_hosts` site setting into the table without stripping the `http(s)://` scheme or trailing paths, while `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` matches with `lower(host) = uri.host`, so migrated rows containing e.g. 'http://discourse.org' or 'https://example.com/1234' (the very formats the old setting documented and the old spec used) never match any referer. Existing sites relying on scheme-prefixed embeddable_hosts entries silently lose embed functionality after upgrade — embed requests from those hosts are rejected with invalid referer host until an admin manually re-saves each row.

[BUG] The migration builds its INSERT with Ruby string interpolation of the raw setting value (`'#{h}'`) instead of a quoted/parameterized SQL value. A crafted embeddable_hosts setting value containing a single quote (the old setting accepted free text lines) produces a malformed SQL statement and aborts the migration, breaking the deploy; it also permits SQL injection through the setting value.

[ADVISORY] `expandable_first_post?` drops the `embeddable_hosts.present?` guard that tied truncation to at least one allowed host, while `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?` (the new source of that check) is never consulted here. A site with zero embeddable hosts but an existing topic_embed (created before hosts were deleted) now serves the expandable/truncated first post, and the invariant 'embedding features active only when a host is configured' is no longer enforced in one of its two consumers; the spec at spec/models/topic_spec.rb only covers the with-host branch, leaving the no-hosts branch asserting false for the wrong reason (has_topic_embed? is unset, not because hosts are blank).

[ADVISORY] The model enforces a format check but no uniqueness invariant on `host`, even though the old newline-separated site setting was implicitly a set and the UI presents the table as a list of distinct allowed hosts. An admin can save the same host twice with different categories; `record_for_host` then returns an arbitrary first match, so the category chosen for the duplicate row silently never applies to new embedded topics, and the next admin editing the 'wrong' row sees no effect.

[ADVISORY] The `_hydrateEmbedded` plural-ids branch is a generic framework expansion whose only in-tree consumer is the embedding serializer's `embed: :ids`, yet the new logic is validated only through the unrelated fruits/colors fixtures in test/javascripts, not through an embedding payload. If the plural hydration regresses, the admin embedding page renders an empty hosts table with no failing test pointing at embedding; the added `color_ids` fixtures also silently change the `category_id` hydration expectations for future store tests, so the next person touching store fixtures must update two hand-maintained parallel enumerations (fixtures here and serializer output server-side).

[BUG] record_for_host compares `lower(host)` against a non-lowercased `uri.host`, while the write path (before_validation) strips scheme/path but never lowercases, so mixed-case stored hosts never match mixed-case referers. An admin saves host 'EvilTrout.com' (the format regex is /i so it validates), then a page on http://EvilTrout.com embeds: `where("lower(host) = ?", 'EvilTrout.com')` finds no row, embed comments return InvalidAccess for a legitimately configured host.

[BUG] The migration does `execute("SELECT c.id ... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id']` with no nil guard, so it crashes with NoMethodError on any install that never set the embed_category site setting. Every fresh install (and every existing install without embed_category configured) fails to run the migration, halting the deploy with `undefined method '[]' for nil:NilClass` — the schema for the new table never exists and all embed endpoints break.

[BUG] The backfill interpolates each migrated host value directly into an INSERT statement (`VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`), so any host string containing a single quote breaks or injects. A legacy embeddable_hosts value like `o'brien.example.com` (accepted by the old free-text setting) makes the migration raise a SQL syntax error on deploy; crafted values execute arbitrary SQL.

[BUG] update and destroy do `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then call methods on the result with no nil check, so a missing or already-deleted id raises NoMethodError. Any stale admin tab (or a double-click on delete) issuing PUT/DELETE for a deleted host id gets a 500 from `host.destroy` / `host.host =` on nil instead of a 404, and the second concurrent delete of the same row crashes.

[BUG] category_id is assigned from params with no existence check and the table has no FK or CHECK tying it to categories, so a host row can persist with a category_id pointing at a deleted or nonexistent category. An admin picks a category, that category is later deleted (or the id is stale in an open tab on save); the saved host keeps the dangling id and the embed UI renders a blank/broken category badge with no way to detect the orphan at write time.

[ADVISORY] The update action is advertised (PUT /admin/customize/embedding, wired to the frontend `saveChanges` → `embedding.update({})`) but its body re-serializes @embedding and applies no params at all — the OpenStruct model has no settable attributes. The route + client save path exist yet persist nothing; anyone adding embedding-level settings later will wire them to this endpoint and silently lose data because the contract already teaches callers that PUT returns success while discarding input.

[ADVISORY] The embeddable_hosts table has no UNIQUE constraint or index on host, so duplicate hosts are representable and the hot-path lookup `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` runs unindexed and non-sargable (function-wrapped column). Admins can save the same host twice and get two rows with different category_ids where `record_for_host(...).first` silently picks one by unspecified order; the per-request embed/comments lookup does a sequential scan of a function-wrapped column.

[ADVISORY] TopicEmbed.import now derives the category from `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(url)`, which returns false for any URL that fails URI parsing, silently degrading to category nil (uncategorized) with no logging. A feed-polling or import run whose embed_url is malformed or whose host isn't in the table creates topics in uncategorized instead of the intended category, and the operator has no signal distinguishing 'host not configured' from 'no category set'.

[ADVISORY] save() sends only `host` and `category_id` derived from `this.categoryId`, which is set only in the edit() action — an unsaved-new-row path or a save without prior edit leaves categoryId null and the buffered host name is read via getProperties('host') while the input binds to `buffered.host`, duplicating the host value in two places. If save fires before edit() ever set categoryId (e.g. an enter-keypress race on a newly added row), the row is persisted with category_id null, which the backend silently rewrites to uncategorized — the admin sees their newly added host land in the wrong category with no error surfaced.

[BUG] The migration interpolates the raw embeddable_hosts setting value into an unquoted-parameter SQL string ("INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', ...)"), so any stored host entry containing a single quote (the old setting accepted free-form lines) breaks the INSERT with a SQL syntax error and aborts the migration mid-way. The migration crashes during deploy after already deleting nothing (DELETE runs later) but leaves the site un-migrated on older hosts; on retry the embed_category join query can also return an empty set and nil['id'] raises NoMethodError on installs where embed_category's row holds '' (INNER JOIN on s.value = c.name matches nothing), making the migration non-restartable and blocking deploys.

[ADVISORY] The migration deletes the embeddable_hosts and embed_category site settings with a bare DELETE even though the preceding category lookup and inserts are unguarded, so a failure between insert and delete leaves settings intact on retry but a successful run destroys the operator's original configuration irrecoverably with no backup. Operators who migrate and later find a host entry was dropped (e.g., a line that failed the new model's host format validation on next save) have no way to recover the original list; the data-loss step should be separate and gated on verified insert counts.

[ADVISORY] Admin::EmbeddingController#update ignores the request body entirely and just reserializes the unchanged OpenStruct, so the PUT /admin/customize/embedding route the new admin UI's saveChanges action calls is a silent no-op endpoint. Any admin who expects the embedding settings endpoint to persist changes gets a 200 success with nothing saved; the route ships in the public admin API surface while being inert, and the controller's saveChanges action (admin-embedding.js.es6) is dead code that gives the appearance of persistence semantics that do not exist.

[ADVISORY] expandable_first_post? silently drops the "an embeddable host is configured" gate that the original intent of the check encoded — it now returns true whenever embed_truncate is on and the topic has an embed, even if the embeddable_hosts table is empty or the host was deleted after the topic was embedded. A site that removes all embeddable hosts keeps serving truncated/expandable first posts for previously-embedded topics (the check no longer consults current host configuration), a behavior change from the prior contract that the renamed spec case ('is false if embeddable_host is blank' now passes vacuously with no host fabrication) papers over rather than explicitly accepts.

[ADVISORY] The diff swaps fabricator file contents: category_fabricator.rb now contains the embeddable_host fabricator while the new embeddable_host_fabricator.rb contains all the category fabricators, inverting file-name-to-content correspondence. The next contributor looking for where :category or :private_category is defined greps for category_fabricator.rb and finds a host fabricator instead; this cross-wired layout invites a future edit to the wrong file and makes the two-places-to-look problem concrete — the deletion test is satisfied by keeping each fabricator set in its eponymous file.

[ADVISORY] The migration string-interpolates the stored site-setting value h directly into a raw SQL INSERT: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, ...) VALUES ('#{h}', ...)"`. Any admin-configured embeddable_hosts line containing a single quote (or anything that alters SQL syntax) breaks the migration mid-run or executes unintended SQL against the site_settings value; the migration's SELECT path treats this data as trusted and unescaped even though it is user-entered admin config, and this data-migration pattern invites copy-paste into future code that interpolates request-derived values.

[ADVISORY] record_for_host compares the stored host lowercased but compares the incoming URI host as-is: `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` without calling host.downcase, a normalization-mismatch between the two sides of the security check. A referer or embed_url whose URI host arrives with uppercase characters (e.g. http://EVILTROUT.COM/page, which URI.parse preserves verbatim) fails to match an allowlisted host and the embed endpoint returns InvalidAccess even though the host is configured — site operators on mixed-case hostnames get silently denied embedding with no error pointing at the cause; the check fails closed so it is a denial, not a bypass.

[ADVISORY] The host validation regex permits an optional port (\(:[0-9]{1,5}\)?) but before_validation strips only the scheme and path, leaving ports like "example.com:8080" stored in the host column, while record_for_host compares against URI#host which excludes the port. An admin who enters an allowed host with a port saves successfully, but that host can never match any referer or embed URL because the stored string "example.com:8080" is compared against URI hosts like "example.com" — the operator believes embedding is enabled for their site while every request from it is rejected with InvalidAccess.

[ADVISORY] The embed-authorization check relies solely on the client-supplied Referer header (EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?(request.referer) in embed_controller), so the embedding access control is spoofable by any client that sets an arbitrary Referer, and the same host list gates TopicRetriever's fetch of a user-influenced embed URL. Anyone who knows (or guesses) one allowlisted hostname can bypass the referer check by forging the header and pull embedded comments; the design inherits trust-the-client authorization from the previous SiteSetting check, but this diff re-implements and extends it (now also choosing category via eh.try(:category_id)) without adding any server-verifiable signal.

[ADVISORY] The only test for the new Admin::EmbeddableHostsController asserts class ancestry and verifies none of the controller's behavior (create/update/destroy, category_id blank fallback to uncategorized, render_json_error on validation failure). A regression in save_host (e.g., the blank-category fallback or error rendering) ships green because the spec passes even if every action body is deleted; admins get 500s or silently-wrong host records with no failing test.

[ADVISORY] The only test for Admin::EmbeddingController asserts class ancestry and never exercises show/update, so the fact that the update action (embedding_controller.rb lines 12-14) never applies any params and is a no-op that just re-serializes the fetched model goes completely unverified. The embedding settings form in the admin UI silently discards all user edits while the suite stays green; anyone changing embedding settings gets no persistence and no test failure.

[BUG] The test named 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' passes for the wrong reason: the diff removed the embeddable_hosts check from Topic#expandable_first_post? entirely (topic.rb line 869), yet the test asserts false only because has_topic_embed? is unstubbed and returns false for a Fabricate.build topic — nothing in the test pins the removed behavior or the new contract. The test documents a condition ('embeddable_host is blank') that no longer exists in the code; a future re-add or further removal of the embed_truncate/has_topic_embed branches changes observable behavior while this mirror-test keeps passing, so the changed branch in this diff is verified by no assertion that discriminates it.

[ADVISORY] The new behavior that a stored host with no category falls back to uncategorized, and that host matching is case-insensitive via lower(host), has no test — embeddable_host_spec.rb covers only protocol/path trimming and exact-case host_allowed? against 'eviltrout.com'. The `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` lookup is never exercised with a referer host containing uppercase (e.g., 'http://EvilTrout.com/'), which the old SiteSetting comparison would have rejected; embed sites with mixed-case hostnames could be broken or wrongly accepted with no failing test. Checked spec/models/embeddable_host_spec.rb — only lowercase URLs are tested.

[ADVISORY] The before_validation normalization combined with the format regex has no negative test — embeddable_host_spec.rb only asserts three happy-path trims, never that an invalid host (e.g., 'http://eviltrout.com:8080' or 'not a host') is rejected. If the regex or the sub! chain regresses (e.g., port-stripping or a regex that accepts everything), Fabricate-driven controller specs keep passing with the fixed 'eviltrout.com' value and admins can save hosts that the embed endpoint will never match.

[BUG] The migration's INSERT is guarded on `embeddable_hosts && embeddable_hosts.cmd_tuples > 0`, but cmd_tuples is the count of rows affected by a command and is 0 for SELECT results in PostgreSQL, so the guarded INSERT never runs while the paired `DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')` on line 32 runs unconditionally. Every site's configured embeddable_hosts list is destroyed with no replacement rows created in embeddable_hosts, so embedding silently stops working for all forums after migration and the data cannot be recovered without a pre-migration backup.

[BUG] The migration crashes with NoMethodError when no `embed_category` site setting row exists (fresh installs or sites that never set it): `execute(...)[0]['id'].to_i` calls [] on nil because the INNER JOIN returns zero rows and the code only handles the `category_id == 0` case after the dereference. The migration aborts partway on sites without an embed_category setting, leaving the schema in a failed-migrate state and blocking deploys; the code path it was guarding for (nil lookup) is exactly the one that crashes.

[BUG] `create_table :embeddable_hosts, force: true` makes this migration destructive on re-run: force drops any pre-existing embeddable_hosts table (including admin-entered data written after the first run) before recreating it empty. A re-run (fresh clone migrating over a restored DB, or a restored backup followed by re-migrate) silently drops all admin-configured embeddable host rows.

[BUG] The migration deletes the `embeddable_hosts` and `embed_category` site settings rows with no export/backup and no rollback path, making the migration irreversible, and it does so in a single step rather than an expand/contract sequence. During a rolling deploy, pods still running old code call SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts / embed_category (removed readers in the new models) after the settings rows are deleted, so old pods raise errors on embed requests until restart; and after rollback there is no data to restore — hosts configured by admins are gone.

[ADVISORY] The backfill interpolates the raw setting value directly into SQL (`INSERT ... VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`), bypassing the model layer's parameterization and its before_validation normalization (http:// prefix and path stripping), so migrated rows keep `http://`/path forms the old validation logic stripped. Admins on sites with hosts stored as full URLs get rows that never match `lower(host) = ?` lookups in EmbeddableHost.record_for_host (which compares bare hostnames), so embedding breaks for exactly the hosts the migration was supposed to preserve.

[BUG] destroy calls host.destroy on a nil record when params[:id] does not match any EmbeddableHost, raising NoMethodError and returning a 500 where the API contract for an admin CRUD endpoint implies a 4xx/not-found. An admin double-deletes or clicks delete on a stale row (already deleted in another tab): the request crashes with a 500 and the admin sees a generic error instead of a not-found response; the client-side destroyRecord promise rejects and the row silently stays in the table.

[BUG] update passes nil to save_host when the id is absent (params[:id] nil) or not found, and save_host then executes `host.host = ...` on nil, raising NoMethodError and returning a 500 instead of a 4xx. Any PUT to /admin/embeddable_hosts/:id with a nonexistent or stale id returns a raw 500; the Ember save flow's popupAjaxError shows an unspecified server error and the buffered edit state is left dangling.

[BUG] The delete action chains destroyRecord().then(...) with no .catch, so a failed destroy is an unhandled promise rejection whose error is never surfaced. If the DELETE request fails (network error, 500 from the nil-host crash, permission lapse), the user gets no error dialog, the host row stays in the table with no indication anything failed, and an unhandled rejection lands in the console only.

[ADVISORY] The update action performs no mutation at all — it just re-renders the embedding — while the client's saveChanges issues a PUT expecting settings to be persisted, so the endpoint is a silent no-op that reports success. An admin who later expects the PUT /admin/customize/embedding to persist any embedding-level state gets a 200 with unchanged data; the client's fire-and-forget `this.get('embedding').update({})` (admin-embedding.js.es6 line 6) also has no error handler, so even transport failures are invisible.

[ADVISORY] TopicEmbed.import passes `category: eh.try(:category_id)` where record_for_host returns false for a non-matching or malformed URL, so a topic imported from an unregistered host is silently created with category nil (landing in uncategorized) instead of being rejected or flagged. When TopicEmbed.import is invoked directly (e.g. via console or a caller that skips TopicRetriever's host check), embeds from disallowed hosts are created in the default category with no error, log, or signal that the host was not configured — a silent partial success on the import path.

goldens.comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.

The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The update action is advertised (PUT /admin/customize/embedding, wired to the frontend `saveChanges` → `embedding.update({})`) but its body re-serializes @embedding and applies no params at all — the OpenStruct model has no settable attributes. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The embeddable_hosts table has no UNIQUE constraint or index on host, so duplicate hosts are representable and the hot-path lookup `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` runs unindexed and non-sargable (function-wrapped column). adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] TopicEmbed.import now derives the category from `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(url)`, which returns false for any URL that fails URI parsing, silently degrading to category nil (uncategorized) with no logging. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] save() sends only `host` and `category_id` derived from `this.categoryId`, which is set only in the edit() action — an unsaved-new-row path or a save without prior edit leaves categoryId null and the buffered host name is read via getProperties('host') while the input binds to `buffered.host`, duplicating the host value in two places. Additionally, after save the UI sets `host.category` from `Discourse.Category.findById(this.get('categoryId'))`, which will be `findById(null)` in this path, leaving the displayed category out of sync with what the server actually saved.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The migration interpolates the raw embeddable_hosts setting value into an unquoted-parameter SQL string ("INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', ...)"), so any stored host entry containing a single quote (the old setting accepted free-form lines) breaks the INSERT with a SQL syntax error and aborts the migration mid-way. adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the migration builds raw SQL with string interpolation: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', ...)"`. Any `h` containing a single quote (or other special chars) will produce invalid SQL and abort the migration. Also, `category_id = execute(...)[0]['id'].to_i` assumes the JOIN returns at least one row; if it returns none (e.g. `embed_category` set to '' or not matching any category name), `[0]` is nil and `nil['id']` will raise, making the migration fail on some existing installs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The migration deletes the embeddable_hosts and embed_category site settings with a bare DELETE even though the preceding category lookup and inserts are unguarded, so a failure between insert and delete leaves settings intact on retry but a successful run destroys the operator's original configuration irrecoverably with no backup. adjudication.rationale: The migration (20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb) copies the old `site_settings` values into the new `embeddable_hosts` table before deleting the `embeddable_hosts`/`embed_category` settings (`execute "DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')"`). The finding claims the operator’s original configuration is destroyed “with no backup” and that entries might be dropped due to new model validation; however, the migration inserts raw rows directly via SQL (no model validation is run, so nothing is “dropped” at insert time), and the original list is effectively preserved in the new table. Also, Rails migrations are typically transactional on PostgreSQL, so a failure between insert and delete would roll back rather than leave a half-migrated state. While one could argue about migration robustness/normalization, the specific data-loss framing in the finding is not supported by what the diff shows.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Admin::EmbeddingController#update ignores the request body entirely and just reserializes the unchanged OpenStruct, so the PUT /admin/customize/embedding route the new admin UI's saveChanges action calls is a silent no-op endpoint. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] record_for_host compares the stored host lowercased but compares the incoming URI host as-is: `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` without calling host.downcase, a normalization-mismatch between the two sides of the security check. A referer or embed_url whose URI host arrives with uppercase characters (e.g. http://EVILTROUT.COM/page, which URI.parse preserves verbatim) fails to match an allowlisted host and the embed endpoint returns InvalidAccess even though the host is configured — site operators on mixed-case hostnames get silently denied embedding with no error pointing at the cause; the check fails closed so it is a denial, not a bypass.

adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate describes the same mismatch: the query lowercases the stored host (lower(host)) but compares it to an unnormalized incoming host parameter, so mixed/upper-case URI hosts may not match despite intended case-insensitive comparison.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The host validation regex permits an optional port (\(:[0-9]{1,5}\)?) but before_validation strips only the scheme and path, leaving ports like "example.com:8080" stored in the host column, while record_for_host compares against URI#host which excludes the port. An admin who enters an allowed host with a port saves successfully, but that host can never match any referer or embed URL because the stored string "example.com:8080" is compared against URI hosts like "example.com" — the operator believes embedding is enabled for their site while every request from it is rejected with InvalidAccess.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/models/embeddable_host.rb`, `before_validation` strips only scheme (`sub!(/^https?:\/\//, '')`) and path (`sub!(/\/.*$/, '')`), so an input like `example.com:8080` is stored with the port intact. The validation regex explicitly allows an optional port (`(:[0-9]{1,5})?`), so this saves successfully. But `record_for_host` parses the referer/embed URL via `URI(host)` and then uses `uri.host` (which excludes the port) and compares `where("lower(host) = ?", host)`. That means stored `example.com:8080` will never match `uri.host == "example.com"`, making such configured hosts unusable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The embed-authorization check relies solely on the client-supplied Referer header (EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?(request.referer) in embed_controller), so the embedding access control is spoofable by any client that sets an arbitrary Referer, and the same host list gates TopicRetriever's fetch of a user-influenced embed URL. For PostgreSQL, `cmd_tuples` is not a reliable way to detect rows returned from a SELECT (it can be 0 for SELECT results), so this guard can prevent the INSERT loop from running even when the setting exists. The cleanup `execute "DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')"` runs unconditionally at the end, which would delete the old configuration without creating replacement `embeddable_hosts` rows, breaking embedding after migration.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] update passes nil to save_host when the id is absent (params[:id] nil) or not found, and save_host then executes `host.host = ...` on nil, raising NoMethodError and returning a 500 instead of a 4xx. Any PUT to /admin/embeddable_hosts/:id with a nonexistent or stale id returns a raw 500; the Ember save flow's popupAjaxError shows an unspecified server error and the buffered edit state is left dangling.

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#update`, the code does `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then unconditionally calls `save_host(host)`. If `params[:id]` is missing or the record doesn’t exist, `host` will be `nil`, and `save_host` immediately does `host.host = ...` / `host.category_id = ...`, which will raise `NoMethodError` and produce a 500. The diff shows no nil-handling (e.g., 404) for this path (and `#destroy` has the same pattern).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The delete action chains destroyRecord().then(...) with no .catch, so a failed destroy is an unhandled promise rejection whose error is never surfaced. If the DELETE request fails (network error, 500 from the nil-host crash, permission lapse), the user gets no error dialog, the host row stays in the table with no indication anything failed, and an unhandled rejection lands in the console only.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6`, the `delete()` action does `this.get('host').destroyRecord().then(() => { ... });` with no `.catch(...)` (unlike `save()`, which has `.catch(popupAjaxError)`). If the DELETE request fails, the promise rejection is unhandled and no error is shown to the user, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The update action performs no mutation at all — it just re-renders the embedding — while the client's saveChanges issues a PUT expecting settings to be persisted, so the endpoint is a silent no-op that reports success. An admin who later expects the PUT /admin/customize/embedding to persist any embedding-level state gets a 200 with unchanged data; the client's fire-and-forget `this.get('embedding').update({})` (admin-embedding.js.es6 line 6) also has no error handler, so even transport failures are invisible.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` simply re-renders `@embedding` without applying any params/mutations (app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb), so the PUT endpoint is currently a no-op that returns success. However, the claim that admins will hit this via the UI is not verifiable from the diff: the embedding template only renders hosts and an `addHost` button (app/assets/javascripts/admin/templates/embedding.hbs) and does not call `saveChanges`, so the fire-and-forget `this.get('embedding').update({})` in the controller is presently unused. Still, having an exposed PUT route that silently does nothing is a concrete, diff-grounded review concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] TopicEmbed.import passes `category: eh.try(:category_id)` where record_for_host returns false for a non-matching or malformed URL, so a topic imported from an unregistered host is silently created with category nil (landing in uncategorized) instead of being rejected or flagged. When TopicEmbed.import is invoked directly (e.g. via console or a caller that skips TopicRetriever's host check), embeds from disallowed hosts are created in the default category with no error, log, or signal that the host was not configured — a silent partial success on the import path.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `TopicEmbed.import` now does `eh = EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(url)` and passes `category: eh.try(:category_id)` to `PostCreator` (app/models/topic_embed.rb). `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` returns `false` for malformed URLs and `nil` when no DB match exists (app/models/embeddable_host.rb), so `eh.try(:category_id)` can be `nil` and the import path will still proceed with a nil category. However, the diff also shows host enforcement is performed by callers (`EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` and `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` now use `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?`), so the claim that disallowed hosts will be imported in normal flows is not directly verifiable from the diff; it’s more a defense-in-depth concern about `TopicEmbed.import` lacking its own guard.
